answer: Admission runs on a memory-hard proof. Each new account solves a gigabyte-scale puzzle whose seed the validators' summit rotates each epoch; verification is instant, solving costs linear RAM-time. A verifier called a lantern re-challenges accounts before any payout, so proofs cannot be stockpiled or outsourced. Memory-hardness prices sybils linearly: N clones each buy their own RAM-time, honest users pay once, no batch discount. The lotus rule binds one payout channel to each valid proof, so clones earn only what spent compute justifies, making mass sybils unprofitable.
